title: Heading of the card that lists how the server is set up (Settings › General). Admins see every line; members fewer.
missing: {{names}} is a comma-separated list of environment variable names, such as "OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_MODEL": keep them as is.
ready: First line of the Service setup card (Settings › General), shown instead of the missing line when no required environment variables are missing: the server is set up for text chat, and a successful chat proves it works.
lines.model: Each status line in Service setup: a label, a colon, then {{line}}, which starts in lowercase and is built from the other keys here; the sentence ends with a period.
lines.telegram: Status line in Service setup: {{line}} is one of the telegram keys, in lowercase.
lines.voice: Status line in Service setup: {{line}} is one of the voice keys, in lowercase.
lines.dataKey: Status line in Service setup about the data key that encrypts stored files and credentials: {{line}} is one of the dataKey keys, in lowercase.
lines.keyIds: Status line in Service setup: {{line}} is one of the keyIds keys, in lowercase.
lines.legacy: "Legacy-sealed": what is still encrypted (sealed) with the old key derived from SESSION_SECRET instead of the data key.
lines.reseal: "Re-seal": encrypting stored data again under the current data key.
lines.keyCheck: Status line in Service setup about the last check of a pasted recovery key: {{line}} is built from the keyCheck keys, in lowercase.
lines.backups: Status line in Service setup: {{line}} is built from the backup keys, in lowercase, joined with semicolons.
lines.plugins: Status line in Service setup about plugins that keep their own storage: {{line}} is built from the plugins keys, in lowercase.
lines.continuous: Status line in Service setup about the continuous copy (Litestream’s copy of the database): {{line}} is its status, in lowercase.
lines.offsite: Status line in Service setup: {{line}} is built from the offsite keys, in lowercase, joined with semicolons.
lines.drill: Status line in Service setup about the restore drill (a scheduled test restore): {{line}} is built from the drill keys, in lowercase.
model.byo: {{label}} is the model's name. "Your own subscription": the person connected their own model plan (bring your own).
model.noneByo: "Account → Inference" names a settings page: keep it matching the Settings nav.
model.none: The "Model: …" status line, lowercase: no AI model is set up yet, and people can’t connect their own.
telegram.notConfigured: The "Telegram: …" status line, lowercase: the Telegram bot isn’t set up. TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is an environment variable name: keep it.
telegram.online: The "Telegram: …" status line, lowercase: the Telegram bot is connected.
telegram.onlineAs: {{bot}} is the Telegram bot's username, shown after @.
telegram.connecting: The "Telegram: …" status line, lowercase: the Telegram bot is connecting right now.
telegram.offline: The "Telegram: …" status line, lowercase: the Telegram bot couldn’t connect.
voice.selfHosted: The "Voice: …" status line, lowercase: voice runs on the workspace’s own servers and is configured.
voice.selfHostedDevices: The server transcribes speech, and the phones or browsers read the replies aloud themselves.
voice.selfHostedNeeds: The "Voice: …" status line, lowercase: self-hosted voice still needs a speech-to-text server that streams over a live connection.
voice.present: The "Voice: …" status line, lowercase: voice is configured.
voice.needs: VOICE_API_KEY and VOICE_MODEL are environment variable names: keep them.
runningOne: Part of a status line, lowercase: a backup or restore drill is running at the moment.
runningNow: Part of a status line, lowercase: a re-seal or a recovery key check is running at the moment.
noneYet: Part of a status line, lowercase: no backup, drill or check has run yet.
failed: Part of a status line, lowercase. {{reason}} is the server's error message, in English, without its final period.
failedAt: Part of a status line, lowercase. {{at}} is a formatted date and time; {{reason}} is the server's error message, in English.
wait.seconds: Short durations inside a status line: {{n}} is a whole number of seconds, minutes or hours. Use your language's usual abbreviations.
wait.minutes: Short duration inside a status line: {{n}} is a whole number of minutes. Use your language’s usual abbreviation.
wait.hours: Short duration inside a status line: {{n}} is a whole number of hours. Use your language’s usual abbreviation.
purposes.inference-credentials: What a kind of encrypted (sealed) data holds, lowercase, used in lists such as "files 3, backups 2".
purposes.data-files: A kind of encrypted (sealed) data, lowercase, used in lists such as "files 3, backups 2": stored files.
purposes.backups: A kind of encrypted (sealed) data, lowercase, used in lists such as "files 3, backups 2": backups.
purposes.push-keys: A kind of encrypted (sealed) data, lowercase: the keys that send push notifications to phones.
purposes.dispatch-credentials: The private key of the GitHub App that coding sessions push with. "GitHub App" is GitHub's product name.
purposes.settings-secrets: A kind of encrypted (sealed) data, lowercase: secrets saved in the workspace’s settings, such as tokens.
purposes.mcp-credentials: MCP is the Model Context Protocol (tool servers for AI agents): keep the acronym.
purposes.workspace-secrets: A kind of encrypted (sealed) data, lowercase: secrets the workspace stores for its socios (AI agents) and tools.
purposes.gateway-log: The log of requests and replies that went through the inference gateway.
dataKey.unsetSealed: The "Data key: …" status line, lowercase. The data key encrypts stored files and credentials. DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS and SESSION_SECRET are environment variable names: keep them. "Sealed" means encrypted.
dataKey.unset: The "Data key: …" status line, lowercase. SESSION_SECRET and DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY are environment variable names: keep them.
dataKey.unknown: The "Data key: …" status line, lowercase. {{count}} is how many items are encrypted with a key the server lacks. DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS is an environment variable name: keep it.
dataKey.resealing: The "Data key: …" status line, lowercase: the key is set, and {{count}} items encrypted with an older key are being encrypted again.
dataKey.set: The "Data key: …" status line, lowercase: the data key is set and nothing needs doing.
backup.every: The "Backups: …" status line, lowercase; its parts are joined with semicolons. {{at}} is a formatted date and time, {{size}} a size such as "5 MB", {{reason}} the server's error message in English.
backup.off: Part of the "Backups: …" status line, lowercase: scheduled backups are turned off.
backup.last: Part of the "Backups: …" status line, lowercase. {{at}} is the formatted date and time of the last backup.
backup.lastSize: Part of the "Backups: …" status line, lowercase. {{at}} is the formatted date and time of the last backup, {{size}} its size, such as "5 MB".
backup.offsiteFailed: Part of the "Backups: …" status line, lowercase. {{reason}} is the server’s error message, in English.
backup.offsiteAt: Part of the "Backups: …" status line, lowercase. {{at}} is the formatted date and time the last backup was copied off-site.
backup.offsiteNone: Part of the "Backups: …" status line, lowercase: no backup was copied to off-site storage yet.
plugins.notYet: The "Plugin data: …" status line about plugins that keep their own storage, lowercase. {{name}} is a plugin's name, {{since}} a formatted date and time, {{reason}} the error in English, {{last}} the plugins.lastAt or plugins.lastNone text.
plugins.undeclared: Part of the "Plugin data: …" status line. {{name}} is the plugin’s name.
plugins.undeclaredSince: "Flagged": when the server first noticed the plugin declares no backup.
plugins.failing: Part of the "Plugin data: …" status line. {{name}} is the plugin’s name, {{reason}} the error in English, {{last}} the plugins.lastAt or plugins.lastNone text.
plugins.failingSince: Part of the "Plugin data: …" status line. {{name}} is the plugin’s name, {{since}} a formatted date and time, {{reason}} the error in English, {{last}} the plugins.lastAt or plugins.lastNone text.
plugins.noReason: Shown as {{reason}} in a plugin backup line when the server gave no error message.
plugins.stale: Part of the "Plugin data: …" status line. {{name}} is the plugin’s name, {{last}} the plugins.lastAt or plugins.lastNone text.
plugins.disabled: Part of the "Plugin data: …" status line. {{name}} is the plugin’s name, {{last}} the plugins.lastAt or plugins.lastNone text.
plugins.disabledSince: Part of the "Plugin data: …" status line. {{name}} is the plugin’s name, {{since}} a formatted date and time, {{last}} the plugins.lastAt or plugins.lastNone text.
plugins.lastAt: Inserted as {{last}} in the plugin backup lines, lowercase. {{at}} is the formatted date and time of the plugin’s last good backup.
plugins.lastNone: Inserted as {{last}} in the plugin backup lines, lowercase: the plugin has no good backup yet.
plugins.allBackedUp: The "Plugin data: …" status line, lowercase, when nothing is wrong.
offsite.off: The "Continuous copy off-site: …" status line, lowercase: how often the continuous copy's files are sent to off-site storage. Parts are joined with semicolons.
offsite.every: Part of the "Continuous copy off-site: …" status line, lowercase: how often files are sent off-site. {{count}} is a number of seconds.
offsite.failed: {{row}} is offsite.inRow, with its leading space, or empty after a single failure.
offsite.failedAt: {{at}} is a formatted date and time; {{row}} is offsite.inRow, with its leading space, or empty after a single failure.
offsite.failedReason: {{row}} is offsite.inRow, with its leading space, or empty after a single failure; {{reason}} is the server’s error message, in English.
offsite.failedAtReason: {{at}} is a formatted date and time; {{row}} is offsite.inRow, with its leading space, or empty; {{reason}} is the server’s error message, in English.
offsite.inRow: Inserted right after "the last send failed" (and its time) when several sends failed in a row; it starts with a space. {{count}} is the number of failures in a row.
offsite.behind: {{waited}} is a short duration from the wait keys, such as "10 min".
offsite.sentUpTo: Part of the "Continuous copy off-site: …" status line, lowercase. {{at}} is the formatted date and time of the newest change sent off-site.
offsite.nothingSent: Part of the "Continuous copy off-site: …" status line, lowercase: nothing was sent off-site yet.
offsite.waiting: Part of the "Continuous copy off-site: …" status line, lowercase. {{count}} is how many files wait to be sent.
drill.every: The "Restore drill: …" status line, lowercase. A restore drill restores the continuous copy into scratch files on a schedule and checks them. {{took}} is a short duration from the wait keys; {{restores}} is a comma-separated list built from the drill.restore keys.
drill.manual: Part of the "Restore drill: …" status line, lowercase: drills are not scheduled and run only when an admin selects "Run drill now".
drill.restoreOffsite: One entry of the list inserted as {{restores}}: a restore from the off-site copy. {{took}} is how long it took, such as "10 min".
drill.restorePoint: A restore to a point in time: {{at}} is that formatted date and time.
drill.restoreLatest: A restore of the newest copy.
drill.passed: Part of the "Restore drill: …" status line, lowercase. {{at}} is a formatted date and time, {{took}} a short duration, {{restores}} the list built from the drill.restore keys. "Live": the database in use.
drill.passedDiffer: Tables that differ from the live database only because of writes made since the copy; this is expected.
drill.unknownError: Shown as the reason when a restore drill failed without an error message.
drill.run: Button: starts a restore drill now, in the background.
drill.running: Label of the "Run drill now" button while the drill runs.
keyIds.none: The "Key ids: …" status line, lowercase: fingerprints of the data keys, so an admin can check an escrowed copy. {{current}} and {{previous}} are short hexadecimal ids.
keyIds.current: The "Key ids: …" status line, lowercase. {{current}} is the current data key’s short hexadecimal id.
keyIds.currentPrevious: The "Key ids: …" status line, lowercase. {{current}} and {{previous}} are the current and previous data keys’ short hexadecimal ids.
legacy.none: The "Legacy-sealed: …" status line, lowercase. SESSION_SECRET is an environment variable name. The recovery kit is the offline copy of the server's secrets.
legacy.byPurpose: One entry of a comma-separated list: {{purpose}} is from the purposes keys, {{n}} how many items.
legacy.items: The "Legacy-sealed: …" status line, lowercase. {{count}} is how many stored items are still encrypted with the old key from SESSION_SECRET (an environment variable name: keep it).
legacy.itemsBy: Like legacy.items; {{by}} is a comma-separated list of the kinds of data with their numbers, built from legacy.byPurpose.
reseal.finished: The "Re-seal: …" status line, lowercase: encrypting older data again under the current data key. {{at}} is a formatted date and time.
reseal.unreadable: Part of the "Re-seal: …" status line, lowercase. {{count}} is how many items are encrypted with a key this server doesn’t have.
reseal.left: Part of the "Re-seal: …" status line, lowercase. {{count}} is how many items wait for the next re-seal run.
reseal.button: Button: starts re-encrypting older data under the current data key.
reseal.busy: Label of the "Re-seal under the data key" button while it runs.
reseal.needsKey: DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is an environment variable name: keep it.
keyCheck.which: The "Recovery key check: …" status line, lowercase: an admin pasted an escrowed data key, and the server tried it on a sample of each kind of sealed data. {{keyId}} is the key's short id, {{at}} a formatted date and time. Which of the server's keys the pasted key turned out to be.
keyCheck.error: The "Recovery key check: …" status line, lowercase. {{keyId}} is the key’s short id, {{which}} one of the keyCheck.which texts, {{at}} a formatted date and time, {{reason}} the error in English.
keyCheck.result: The "Recovery key check: …" status line, lowercase; the _failed form when the key didn’t open the samples. {{keyId}} is the key’s short id, {{which}} a keyCheck.which text, {{at}} a formatted date and time, {{purposes}} a list built from keyCheck.opened and keyCheck.nothingToTry.
keyCheck.nothingToTry: One entry of the list in the recovery key check line: {{purpose}} is from the purposes keys, and there was no item of that kind to try the key on.
keyCheck.opened: {{purpose}} is from the purposes keys; {{opened}} of {{sampled}} sampled items opened with the key.
recovery.label: Label of a password field where an admin pastes a data key from escrow to check it.
recovery.hint: "Escrow": the safe place outside the server where a copy of the key is kept.
recovery.verify: Button next to the recovery key field: checks the pasted key.
recovery.checking: Label of the Verify button while the recovery key is being checked.
